chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About a man who comes to his slave-girl during the daytime in the month of Ramadan while traveling, so he said: “This one has not recognized the due right of the month of Ramadan; indeed, he has in the night a long span.”

He said: I said to him, “Does he not have the right to eat, drink, and shorten?” He said: “Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted the traveler a concession in breaking the fast and shortening out of mercy and lightening because of the place of fatigue, hardship, and the roughness of travel. But He did not grant him a concession in having intercourse with women during travel by day in the month of Ramadan; and He made obligatory upon him the qaḍāʾ of the fasting, and He did not make obligatory upon him the qaḍāʾ of completing the salat when he returns from his travel.”
Then he said: “And the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is not subject to analogy, and indeed when I travel in the month of Ramadan, I do not eat all the food, nor do I drink to full quenching.”

key_terms.تُقَاسُ: measured by analogy; used here in negation to reject legal analogy in this matter
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose daytime sanctity remains significant even during travel
key_terms.قَضَاءَ ٱلصِّيَامِ: making up the missed fast afterward
key_terms.مُجَامَعَةِ ٱلنِّسَاءِ: sexual intercourse with women, here stated as not permitted by day in Ramadan during travel
key_terms.ٱلسَّفَرِ: travel, the condition in which some legal concessions are granted
key_terms.ٱلسُّنَّةُ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition), which is not established through analogy
key_terms.ٱلْإِفْطَارِ: breaking the fast, a concession granted to the traveler

ai.seo_question: Can a traveler in Ramadan have intercourse during the daytime if eating and drinking are permitted?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that although a traveler is given a concession to break the fast and shorten the salat (prayer), this does not extend to sexual relations during the daytime of Ramadan. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام emphasizes the sanctity of the month, distinguishes between divinely legislated concessions, and states that the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is not to be derived through analogy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1986 - Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who engages with his concubine during the day in the Month of Ramadan while traveling.
The Imam (as) responded: "This person has not recognized the sanctity of the Month of Ramadan, for he has a long stretch of permissible time at night."

The questioner asked: "Is it not permissible for him to eat, drink, and shorten his prayer while traveling?"
The Imam (as) replied: "Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, granted the traveler the concession to break the fast and shorten the prayer out of mercy and ease, considering the hardship, exhaustion, and difficulties of travel. However, He did not permit engaging in sexual relations during the day while traveling in the Month of Ramadan. For this, He has mandated the fast's make-up (qada) but has not required the make-up of full prayers when the traveler returns home."
The Imam then added: "Religious practices are not subject to analogy. When I travel during the Month of Ramadan, I do not consume all food or drink in full measure."
